sources: docs/research.md section 6 for advisories not present in OSV (verified: false)

advisories.component: std/algebra emulated scalar multiplication (fake-GLV); std/signature/ecdsa incl. P-256
advisories.summary: Fake-GLV scalar-multiplication hint result is not checked to be on the curve, which lets a prover forge ECDSA / P-256 verification in-circuit.
advisories.action: Upgrade to v0.16.4 or later, recompile every affected circuit and regenerate proving and verifying keys; redeploy any verifier contract built from the old keys.

advisories.component: std (emulated arithmetic, torus, GLV, uints lookups for SHA2/Keccak, pairing Miller loop, comb scalar mul)
advisories.summary: Eleven std-library issues where a hint output is consumed without a binding or range constraint (emulated carry not range-checked, unconstrained torus scale, unbound GLV sub-scalars, remainder vs runtime modulus, uints lookup key collision, Miller loop with Q = 0, comb top bit).
advisories.action: Upgrade to v0.16.2 or later (v0.16.4 also fixes GHSA-7fx8), recompile affected circuits and regenerate keys and verifier contracts.

advisories.component: std/algebra pairing G2 membership (IsOnTwist vs AssertIsOnTwist)
advisories.summary: A G2 subgroup / twist check is computed but its result is discarded, so points off the twist are accepted.
advisories.action: Upgrade past v0.15.0, recompile affected circuits and regenerate keys. Research notes give the fix as 'after v0.15.0'; confirm the exact version on the advisory page.

advisories.summary: The scalar decomposition used by fake-GLV converges very slowly for some inputs, so a prover that accepts untrusted witnesses can be stalled (denial of service).
advisories.action: Upgrade gnark to v0.13.0 or later, or upgrade gnark-crypto to a version with commit 56600883. No recompilation is needed: the bug is in a hint.

advisories.summary: Signature scalar S is not checked to satisfy 0 <= S < order, so signatures are malleable; nullifiers or replay keys derived from (R, S) can be double-spent.
advisories.action: Upgrade to v0.14.0 or later and recompile; never derive nullifiers or replay protection from signature bytes.

advisories.component: backend/groth16 and backend/plonk deserialization (VerifyingKey, Proof ReadFrom)
advisories.summary: Deserializing a crafted verifying key or proof allocates attacker-chosen sizes and can exhaust memory.
advisories.action: Upgrade to v0.11.1 or later (the Go vuln DB entry GO-2024-3244 lists v0.12.0); do not deserialize keys or proofs from untrusted sources without size limits.

advisories.component: backend/groth16 commitment extension (more than one commitment)
advisories.summary: The same sigma is used for the proof of knowledge of every Groth16 commitment, so a prover can fix all but one commitment before choosing the witness; Groth16 with more than one commitment is unsound.
advisories.action: Upgrade to v0.11.0 or later, recompile, rerun setup and redeploy the verifier.

advisories.component: backend/groth16 commitment extension (commitments to private witnesses)
advisories.summary: Groth16 commitments to private witness values are binding but not hiding, so a verifier can confirm guesses of committed secrets; zero knowledge is lost.
advisories.action: Upgrade to v0.11.0 or later, recompile, rerun setup and redeploy the verifier.

advisories.component: std/rangecheck (used by field emulation, ECDSA, recursion)
advisories.summary: The range checker did not account for a short top partition, so inputs up to 16 bits wider than requested were accepted.
advisories.action: Upgrade to v0.9.2 or later and recompile.

advisories.summary: The KZG batch-opening randomness was derived from only the first 32 bytes of the verifier state, so a third party can derive a different valid proof for the same public inputs (the 'Last Challenge' attack).
advisories.action: Regenerate the PLONK Solidity verifier with v0.9.1 or later and redeploy it.

advisories.component: frontend API Cmp / IsLess, bits.ToBinary / api.ToBinary at full width
advisories.summary: Full-width binary decomposition accepts both a and a + r, so Cmp / IsLess can prove a < b when a > b.
advisories.action: Upgrade to v0.9.0 or later and recompile; on older versions use std/math/cmp with a known bound.
